eligibility_reason: RP:CB Replication Study reporting new experimental data from replications of Figures 1A, 2B and 4A of Hatzivassiliou et al. (2010, Nature), as pre-specified in the Registered Report (Bhargava et al., 2016).

effects.original_title: RAF inhibitors prime wild-type RAF to activate the MAPK pathway and enhance growth
effects.original_authors: Hatzivassiliou, G; Song, K; Yen, I; Brandhuber, B; Anderson, D; Alvarado, R; Ludlam, M; Stokoe, D; Gloor, S; Vigers, G; Morales, T; Aliagas, I; Liu, B; Sideris, S; Hoeflich, K; Jaiswal, B; Seshagiri, S; Koeppen, H; Belvin, M; Friedman, L; Malek, S
effects.replication_study: Protocol 1 / Figure 1A replication: cell viability dose-response assay (A375, HCT116, MeWo)
effects.outcome: Cell viability (EC50) after 4-day treatment with RAF inhibitors PLX4720 / GDC-0879 or MEK inhibitor PD0325901
effects.contrast: BRAF(V600E) cells (A375) vs mutant RAS (HCT116) and wild-type RAF/RAS (MeWo) cells; RAF inhibitors vs MEK inhibitor
effects.timepoint: 4 days (96 hr) after start of treatment
effects.description: The RAF inhibitors PLX4720 and GDC-0879 selectively inhibited proliferation of BRAF(V600E) cancer cell lines but not RAF wild-type or RAS-mutant lines, whereas the MEK inhibitor PD0325901 inhibited proliferation of all of them (Figure 1A).
effects.citation_sentence: Using the same ATP-competitive RAF inhibitors as Hatzivassiliou et al. (2010), we aimed to independently replicate an experiment testing the selective nature of RAF inhibitors in inhibiting proliferation of BRAF(V600E) cells. ... This experiment was comparable to what was reported in Figure 1A of Hatzivassiliou et al. (2010) and described in Protocol 1 in the Registered Report (Bhargava et al., 2016).
effects.evidence: Results, 'Assessing cell viability...' (pp. 6-7): "To summarize, for this experiment we found results that were in the same direction as the original study." Abstract: "We found two unrelated RAF inhibitors, PLX4720 or GDC-0879, selectively inhibited BRAF(V600E) cell proliferation, while the MEK inhibitor, PD0325901, inhibited ... cancer cell proliferation, similar to the original study (Figure 1A...)"
effects.notes: No inferential test; classification from authors' 'same direction'/'similar to the original study' statements. Replication used one cell line per genotype vs the original's panel; A375 RAF-inhibitor EC50s (0.20/0.23 uM) lower than original estimates (0.5/0.3 uM) and outside replication 95% CI, but authors call overall EC50s consistent. RAF-inhibitor selectivity and MEK-inhibitor pan-activity coded as one claim (one panel, Fig 1A); a coder splitting them would code both success.

effects.original_title: RAF inhibitors prime wild-type RAF to activate the MAPK pathway and enhance growth
effects.original_authors: Hatzivassiliou, G; Song, K; Yen, I; Brandhuber, B; Anderson, D; Alvarado, R; Ludlam, M; Stokoe, D; Gloor, S; Vigers, G; Morales, T; Aliagas, I; Liu, B; Sideris, S; Hoeflich, K; Jaiswal, B; Seshagiri, S; Koeppen, H; Belvin, M; Friedman, L; Malek, S
effects.replication_study: Protocol 2 / Figure 2B replication: HCT116 dox-inducible BRAF or CRAF shRNA cells treated with PLX4720
effects.outcome: Phospho-MEK (normalized to total MEK and vehicle) induction after 1 hr PLX4720 treatment
effects.contrast: CRAF shRNA induced vs not induced, and BRAF shRNA induced vs not induced (shRNA x dox interaction)
effects.description: In RAS-mutant HCT116 cells, knockdown of CRAF but not BRAF reversed PLX4720-induced MEK phosphorylation, showing the paradoxical MAPK activation is CRAF-dependent (Figure 2B).
effects.citation_sentence: To test the role that CRAF and BRAF have in signalling to MEK in non-BRAF(V600E) cells after RAF inhibitor treatment HCT116 cells engineered to stably express dox inducible shRNA (Hoeflich et al., 2006) were utilized. This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 2B of Hatzivassiliou et al. (2010) and described in Protocol 2 in the Registered Report (Bhargava et al., 2016).
effects.evidence: Results, 'Assessing CRAF and BRAF roles...' (pp. 7-9): interaction F(1,80) = 6.95, p = 0.010; CRAF contrast t(80) = 3.66, corrected p = 0.00091, d = 1.13; BRAF contrast corrected p > 0.99. "To summarize, for this experiment we found results that were in the same direction as the original study and statistically significant where predicted." Abstract: "knockdown of CRAF, but not BRAF, in mutant RAS cells attenuated the phospho-MEK induction observed after PLX4720 treatment, similar to the original study"
effects.notes: Dose-response shape differed (peak induction at lowest dose rather than dose-dependent increase), but the CRAF-dependence claim was supported. PLX4720 and GDC-0879 arms of Fig 2B coded as separate entries because the replication reports them as separately run and analysed experiments with separate conclusions; a coder treating both drugs as one claim would code a single inconclusive entry (results differ across drugs).

effects.original_title: RAF inhibitors prime wild-type RAF to activate the MAPK pathway and enhance growth
effects.original_authors: Hatzivassiliou, G; Song, K; Yen, I; Brandhuber, B; Anderson, D; Alvarado, R; Ludlam, M; Stokoe, D; Gloor, S; Vigers, G; Morales, T; Aliagas, I; Liu, B; Sideris, S; Hoeflich, K; Jaiswal, B; Seshagiri, S; Koeppen, H; Belvin, M; Friedman, L; Malek, S
effects.replication_study: Protocol 2 / Figure 2B replication: HCT116 dox-inducible BRAF or CRAF shRNA cells treated with GDC-0879
effects.outcome: Phospho-MEK (normalized to total MEK and vehicle) induction after 1 hr GDC-0879 treatment
effects.contrast: CRAF shRNA induced vs not induced, and BRAF shRNA induced vs not induced
effects.description: In RAS-mutant HCT116 cells, knockdown of CRAF but not BRAF reversed GDC-0879-induced MEK phosphorylation, as for PLX4720 (Figure 2B).
effects.citation_sentence: The role of CRAF and BRAF was also tested in the same experimental set-up with GDC-0879. ... For comparison, the original study reported depletion of CRAF, but not BRAF, reversed the phospho-MEK induction after GDC-0879 treatment, similar to what was reported for PLX4720.
effects.evidence: Results (pp. 9-10): BRAF contrast U = 131, corrected p = 0.048, Cliff's delta = -0.41; CRAF contrast U = 247, corrected p > 0.99. "To summarize, for this experiment we found results that were not in the same direction as the original study and not statistically significant where predicted." "Interpretation of these results should take into consideration that GDC-0879 did not appreciably activate MEK in the BRAF shRNA cell line". Abstract: "The original study reported analogous results with GDC-0879, which was not observed in this replication, although unexpected control results confound the interpretation."
effects.notes: Authors state the original result was not observed (failure reading), but also that unexpected control results (no pMEK induction in uninduced BRAF shRNA cells, possibly genetic drift) confound interpretation; per codebook tiebreakers (validity concerns; failure-vs-inconclusive doubt -> inconclusive) coded inconclusive. A second coder could plausibly code failure. Not a reversal: the authors do not describe an opposite finding.

effects.original_authors: Hatzivassiliou, G; Song, K; Yen, I; Brandhuber, B; Anderson, D; Alvarado, R; Ludlam, M; Stokoe, D; Gloor, S; Vigers, G; Morales, T; Aliagas, I; Liu, B; Sideris, S; Hoeflich, K; Jaiswal, B; Seshagiri, S; Koeppen, H; Belvin, M; Friedman, L; Malek, S
effects.replication_study: Protocol 3 / Figure 4A replication: in vitro BRAF-CRAF kinase-domain heterodimerization (GST-CRAF immunoprecipitation) assay
effects.outcome: Co-immunoprecipitation of BRAF (wild-type or V600E) kinase domain with GST-CRAF kinase domain
effects.contrast: PLX4720, GDC-0879 or AMP-PCP vs vehicle (DMSO), for wild-type BRAF vs BRAF(V600E) kinase domains
effects.timepoint: not applicable: in vitro binding assay (1 hr incubation)
effects.description: Purified CRAF and BRAF kinase domains formed a stable complex that was destabilized by PLX4720 (and AMP-PCP) and stabilized by GDC-0879 for wild-type BRAF, while the compounds did not alter CRAF-BRAF(V600E) interaction (Figure 4A).
effects.citation_sentence: Using purified recombinant proteins, we aimed to replicate whether the CRAF kinase domain forms a stable complex with the BRAF kinase domain and if the ATP-competitive RAF inhibitors modulate this dimerization. This experiment tested whether RAF priming is mediated by the inhibitors' conformational effects on the RAF kinase domain and is similar to what was reported in Figure 4A of Hatzivassiliou et al. (2010) and described in Protocol 3 in the Registered Report (Bhargava et al., 2016).
effects.evidence: Results, 'Biochemical heterodimerization assay...' (pp. 12-16): BRAF bound Protein-A-agarose beads without GST-CRAF; drug effects were on BRAF-bead binding. "These data, while unable to address whether, under the conditions of the original study, the same observations could be observed, highlight the challenges encountered during this replication attempt." Abstract: "Although we were unable to conduct the experiment as planned, we observed differential binding of BRAF by RAF inhibitors; however, it was between BRAF and beads, independent of CRAF."
effects.notes: Experiment was run with new data, but a negative control (no GST-CRAF) showed BRAF pulled down by beads, so the CRAF-BRAF dimerization claim could not be tested; drug-dependent pattern mirrored the original but was CRAF-independent. Coded one entry (the assay could not address any sub-claim: basal complex, PLX4720 destabilization, GDC-0879 stabilization, no effect on V600E). Alternative readings: failure (basal complex not CRAF-dependent) or treating it as not a completed replication. Replication_type: authors call the project a 'direct replication', but antibodies, CRAF supplier/activating mutations (Y340E/Y341E vs Y340D/Y341D) and BRAF construct length (417-766 vs 432-726) differed, and AZ-628 was omitted; close experiment is a plausible alternative.
